sentences.text: learn English for real life situations. Today, we have a fun and exciting topic, going to
a concert. Imagine you are at a live concert or a music festival. You need to buy a ticket,
find your seat, order food and drinks, talk about the music, meet new people, and stay safe.
But how do you say these things in English? Don't worry. In this episode, I will teach you
useful English phrases that will help you buy a concert ticket, VIP versus regular tickets.
Find your seat or standing area, order food and drinks, talk about the concert and music,
make friends and meet new people, stay safe and ask for help. What to do if you get lost?
Fun things to do after the concert. By the end of this episode, you will feel more confident
speaking English at a concert. Let's get started. Buying a concert ticket, VIP versus regular tickets.
Before you go to a concert, you need to buy a ticket. You can buy it online or at the ticket
office. But do you know the difference between VIP and regular tickets? VIP ticket perks.
Closer to the stage, exclusive entrance, free drinks or snacks, meet and greet with the artist,
comfortable seating, regular ticket perks, more affordable, general standing area or seats,
same music experience, common phrases, how much is a VIP ticket? What does a VIP ticket include?
Can I buy a regular ticket? Are there any discounts available? Do you have student tickets?
What time does the concert start? Can I pay by credit card?
Example conversation. Hello? How much is a ticket for the concert? It's $50 for a standard ticket
and $150 for VIP. What does the VIP ticket include? It includes front row seats and free drinks.
That sounds great. I'll take a VIP ticket.
Tip, buy your ticket early because some concerts sell out quickly, finding your seat or spot.
When you enter the concert venue, you need to find your seat or a good place to stand.
Common phrases. Where is section B? Can you help me find my seat? Is this seat taken?
Where is the standing area? Where is the best place to see the stage? Excuse me, can I pass through?
Example conversation. Excuse me, where is section B? It's on the left, near the stage.
Thank you. Tip, if you have a standing ticket, arrive early to get a good spot. What to do if you get
lost at a concert? Concert venues can be big and crowded, so it's easy to get lost.
Common phrases. Excuse me, where is the exit? I can't find my seat. Can you help me?
Can I use your phone? Is there a lost and found? Where is the security office?
Example conversation. Excuse me, I lost my friend. What should I do? You can wait near the entrance
or use the lost and found. Thank you. Tip, agree on a meeting point with your friends before the
concert starts. Ordering food and drinks. Common phrases. Can I have a bottle of water?
Do you sell soft drinks? How much is a beer? Can I have a burger and fries? Is there a vegetarian
option? Do you accept cash or card? Example conversation. Do you have soft drinks?
Yes, we have cola, lemonade, and orange juice. I'll take a cola, please. That's $5. Here you go.
Tip, some concerts don't allow outside food and drinks. Talking about the concert and music.
Common phrases. The band is amazing. I love this song. What's your favorite song?
The energy here is great. This is the best concert ever. Example conversation.
Wow, the band is amazing. Yes, I love this song. Me too. Let's sing along. Tip, if you don't know
the lyrics, just dance and enjoy the music. What to do after the concert? The concert is over,
but the night isn't. Here are some fun things you can do. Buy concert merchandise, T-shirts,
posters, CDs, take pictures with friends, get an autograph from the artist, if possible.
Go out for a late night meal. Talk about the concert with new friends.
Common phrases. Let's buy a T-shirt. Where can we get a taxi? I love this concert.
Let's come again next year. Example conversation. That was amazing. Let's buy some merch.
